name: Executive function
summary: Executive function is an umbrella for related higher-level processes involved in goal-directed regulation, commonly including updating working memory, shifting between tasks or rules, and inhibiting prepotent responses.

includes: everyday supports for planning, initiation, switching, memory, and inhibition
excludes: a moral judgement about effort or character
a direct one-to-one reading from a laboratory task to daily life

claims.text: Updating, shifting, and inhibition show both shared variance and separability in a foundational adult latent-variable study.
No single factor structure consistently fits executive-function measures across all ages and samples.

sources.citation: Miyake, A. et al. The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks (2000).
Karr, J. E. et al. The unity and diversity of executive functions: A systematic review and re-analysis of latent variable studies (2018).

uncertainties.question: Which factor models are valid across ages, cultures, neurotypes, and measurement methods?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: A model can appear universal when it reflects a task set or sampled population.

uncertainties.question: How well do task scores predict person-defined functioning in real environments?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: Laboratory performance may not identify barriers or effective accommodations.

perspectives.summary: Executive functions are correlated but partly separable processes rather than one unitary faculty.

relations.note: Executive-function constructs are often studied in ADHD but do not define the whole condition.
Executive demands can be relevant to autistic daily life but profiles vary.
Cognitive performance can depend on sensory load and environment.

questions: Which demand is externalised or reduced?
What setup and maintenance burden remains?
Is transfer to everyday outcomes demonstrated?
Are privacy and notification burden acceptable?
Can instructions, time, sequencing, or interruption demands be redesigned?
Does advice distinguish inability, overload, competing demands, and motivation?
Is failure blamed on the user?

provenance.method: Structured synthesis of cited public sources; no community review yet
